design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 1 of membership_benefits_desk (Northbeam Circle membership benefits desk). Revision 2,
rewritten after the source-layer audit at
env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/audits/policy_task/membership_benefits_desk/ returned RED on all four
relationships. Every figure below is from the revision-2 harness run recorded under STEP 5, and the arithmetic of
the standard solution has been re-derived from that run rather than written out by hand.

STEP 0. DRAW AND ASSET LEDGER.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/membership_benefits_desk --task 1 printed
{"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 4]}. The tree has two prerequisite
problems besides the root and its three computations carry 6, 4 and 5 declared factors:
membership_ext_purchase_points_accrual 6, membership_ext_points_expiry_sweep 4,
membership_ext_points_redemption_release 5. Occupied by task 0 and untouched here: the three benefit-credit
policies with their three tools and the event types membership_dues_payment, membership_benefit_grant and
membership_benefit_redeem. This task claims the whole reward-points side: the points a purchase earned, the
expiry sweep and the release of points on a redemption, with the event types membership_points_accrue,
membership_points_expire and membership_points_redeem and three fresh tools. Between them the two tasks claim
every extended policy of the difficulty and share no policy, tool or event type.

DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: "We have the invoice for the four laptops open on the account and I want to put our
Circle points against it — use whatever they're worth." Scored core parameter: the points the redemption spends
(23,900). Two problems stand between the request and that figure, neither mentioned by the customer. (1) The
points a redemption spends are settled only after the ledger carries an earning entry for every purchase already
billed on the profile — three orders stand billed, the standing supply order and the August board order each
carry their earning entries, and the laptop order of 20 August carries none, so the live balance is short by
18,080 and the answer without it is 14,900. (2) No points are released until the balance carries the sweep entry
owed for the calendar year the handling day falls in — the ledger carries sweeps for the calendar years 2023 and
2025 and none for 2026, while 24,000 points earned in November 2023 have outlived the life the tier gives a
point, so the live balance is read over the wrong window and the answer is 43,000. Depth: surface goal -> the
points released -> the live balance -> the earning entry that is missing and the sweep that is owed. Breadth: the
three computations read the membership points ledger across three years, the profile's order ledger, the
ShieldCare fleet plan, the TechWorks deployment, the Northbeam business account's store credit postings and the
return authorisation on one of the four laptops.

WHY THE CUSTOMER'S OWN WRITE IS THE REDEMPTION. The reward point balance is the member's own property, and
spending it disposes of the member's own position rather than performing a service on the record: the desk can
work out how many points may be released and unlock the redemption, but it cannot give the business's points away
on its behalf. It completes on the call — the points stand on the balance, the entry lands at once and the
reference comes straight back. What stays with the agent is the retailer's own bookkeeping: booking the points a
purchase earned and sweeping the points that have outlived their life.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- membership_points_accrual and membership_combo_protection_interaction both govern membership_points_accrue and
  neither declares structured eligibility, so both enter base_preconditions as policy_scope. Five clauses of
  membership_points_accrual are superseded and named in overwrite: the whole-spend rate clause, the qualifying
  merchandise spend clause (the extended rule brings the TechWorks labour into the same spend), the calendar-year
  cap clause (replaced by a rolling twelve-month cap), the half-up rounding clause (the extended rule states
  half to the nearest even point, which is what RND produces), and the clause on points for a purchase later
  returned (the extended rule takes the goods that went back off the same spend instead of booking a goodwill
  adjustment afterwards, which is what leaves nothing owed on the return in this world). Inherited and
  respected: nothing is earned while the membership stands in grace on a tier that suspends benefits or once it
  has lapsed (the record stands active), and the yearly points cap is applied (84,800 earned in the window
  against a cap of 400,000).
- membership_points_expiry governs membership_points_expire. Its gate sweepable_membership_state holds: the
  record stands active. Its point-life sentence is superseded and named in overwrite; the oldest-points-first
  rule and the one-entry-per-sweep-year rule are inherited, and the extended rule states in terms what a sweep
  year is: the calendar year the day the forfeiture is booked falls in.
- membership_points_redemption governs membership_points_redeem. Its gate active_for_redemption holds. Two
  clauses are superseded and named in overwrite: the whole-blocks clause (replaced by the order sentence, which
  states the share, the hold-backs, the cap and the blocks in one fixed order) and the clause listing the forms a
  redemption may take (replaced by the sentence that a redemption put against a charge already standing on the
  profile is taken as an instant discount rather than as a certificate). Inherited: points are redeemed only
  while the membership stands active, points may never be redeemed against dues or paid out as cash (the cap here
  is an order balance, not dues), and the value of a redemption is the tier's value per hundred points, which the
  extended rule uses in both directions and at one single rate for every amount held back.
- No time gate applies to any of the three writes, so temporal_feasibility is [].

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The root's object is one redemption against one invoice: purchase order KES-4471-0908, the
four laptops delivered to the dock on 27 August, of which one went straight back. The accrual's object is the
same order read as an earning occasion — the merchandise line of 4,800.00 billed on 20 August, the promotional
discount of 480.00 credited against it, the 1,200.00 refund authorised on the machine that went back, and the
deployment labour of 1,400.00 on the TechWorks agreement the profile holds. The sweep's object is the pool that
has outlived its life: the 24,000 points earned on 10 November 2023. Rows deliberately excluded: the 5,600.00
board line of 10 August, inside the twelve-month window and outside the month the lines are counted over, and the
2023 sweep of 4,000 points, outside the twenty-four months the earlier-sweep offset reads.

CROSS-CATEGORY OBJECT DISCIPLINE (revision 2). This is the finding that mattered most, and the fix is structural.
Nothing is read now by "the first holding of that category that matches the customer": every cross-category read
is either an aggregate over a named ledger and window, which the rule states as an aggregate over the profile's
records, or a read of a category the world holds exactly one record of, which the rule names in those words. The
order reads are all ledger aggregates — the merchandise lines billed to the profile in the window, the discounts
credited in it, the payments taken in it, and what stands unsettled on the profile's orders as charges less
credits less payments — so the profile may hold three orders and no scored figure moves if the rows are
re-serialised in any order. The department bonus no longer reads an order at all: it reads the department of the
item the one TechWorks agreement was carried out on. The returns, protection, service and credit reads each name
"the ... the profile holds", and initial_state carries exactly one return_authorizations, one protection_plans,
one service_agreements and one credit_accounts row for this customer.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
root: membership_ext_points_redemption_release (the customer's surface request).
edge 1: redemption <- accrual, kind value_input, gate earned_in_life, form state, sentence carried by the root's
  own rule: "The points a redemption spends are settled only after the ledger carries an earning entry for every
  purchase already billed on the profile." Four-point test: (1) "only after"; (2) a record-visible state — an
  earning entry standing on the ledger against a purchase already billed — with no action, performer or tool
  named; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) exactly the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty
  books an earning entry. Resolved by book_purchase_points_235cc6ac (owner=agent). False at frozen_time: the
  laptop order stands billed and no earning entry names it, the eight oldest entries naming the standing supply
  order placed 2023-10-15 and the ninth naming the August board order. Deletion sensitivity: skipping it leaves
  the root at 14,900 instead of 23,900.
edge 2: redemption <- sweep, kind value_input, gate swept_in_life, form state, sentence carried by the root's own
  rule: "No points are released until the balance carries the sweep entry owed for the calendar year the handling
  day falls in." Four-point test: (1) "until"; (2) a record-visible state — a points expiry entry standing on the
  balance for that sweep year, which the sweep's own rule defines as the calendar year the forfeiture is booked
  in; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) exactly the edge's condition, one named year rather than an open
  quantifier. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a sweep entry. Resolved by
  sweep_expired_points_bcca39ef (owner=agent). False at frozen_time: the ledger's expiry entries carry 2023 and
  2025; none carries 2026. Deletion sensitivity: skipping it leaves the root at 52,100 instead of 23,900.
topological order: the accrual and the sweep in either order, then the release; the two leaves were run in both
orders and give identical figures and an identical terminal hash (see ORDER UNIQUENESS).
The tool layer validates nothing: each of the three tools reads the membership row only for the owning customer
and the tier to stamp on its entry, then writes; none checks a balance, a block, a sweep year already carried or
anything owed on another line.

FACTOR CARD — membership_ext_purchase_points_accrual (6 factors; gold 18,080; whole baseline 20,800).
- counted_line_window (method, cross_difficulty=orders): merchandise billed in the month with a payment taken on
  the profile's orders in that month -> the lines of that month; nothing billed in the month but lines in the
  three months -> those three months; otherwise the twelve months. The baseline paragraph states the
  twelve-month window, which is the fall-through, so the declared baseline of 12 is what a reader of the
  computation document alone takes. World: 4,800.00 billed 2026-08-20 with 2,320.00 taken on 2026-08-28 -> the
  month. Baseline 12 pulls in the 5,600.00 board line: 40,480.
- discount_netted (method, cross_difficulty=orders): a promotional discount credited inside the window -> the
  lines less it; no promotional discount but a price match -> the lines less that; otherwise the lines as they
  stand. World: 480.00 -> 4,320.00. Baseline 20,000.
- returned_goods_taken_off (parameter, cross_difficulty=returns): the return inspected or settled with a refund
  authorised in the three months -> that refund off the spend; authorised or received with no refund yet -> the
  purchase price recorded on it; otherwise nothing. World: inspected with 1,200.00 authorised 2026-09-07 ->
  1,200.00 off. Baseline 22,880. This factor is also how base's "points on a purchase that is later returned"
  clause is honoured: the points are never booked on the machine that went back.
- work_brought_into_spend (parameter, cross_difficulty=service): the agreement completed with labour charged in
  the month -> that labour; completed with no labour in the month -> the least labour billed at its rate;
  otherwise nothing. World: 1,400.00 -> 1,400.00. Baseline 12,480.
- department_bonus_rate (parameter, cross_difficulty=service): the item the agreement was carried out on in
  computing, mobile or home theatre -> the tier's electronics bonus 1.5; a major appliance -> 1.0; otherwise
  none. World: the deployment was carried out on a laptop -> 1.5. Baseline 11,300.
- volume_rate_uplift (parameter): spend reaching the tier's qualifying figure with four or more occasions -> 0.5;
  reaching the mid share but not the figure with two or more -> 0.25; otherwise none. World: 42,400.00 over five
  occasions -> 0.5. Baseline 15,820.

FACTOR CARD — membership_ext_points_expiry_sweep (4 factors; gold 9,000; whole baseline 30,400).
- point_life_window (method): active with an earning occasion in the three months -> the tier's expiry months and
  the active member extension together (30); not active with none -> the expiry months less the dormancy
  reduction (18); otherwise the expiry months (24). The fall-through tier now carries a method and nothing else.
  World: active with an occasion on 2026-08-20 -> 30, leaving only the 24,000 of 2023-11-10 aged. Baseline 24
  also ages the 19,000 of 2024-04-22 and the 12,400 of 2024-08-15: 40,400.
- spend_set_against_aged_pool (method): a redemption in the twelve months with the record active -> the points
  spent in that window; none but a transfer on the ledger -> the points transferred; otherwise every point spent.
  World: the 5,000-point transfer of 2026-04-15 -> 5,000. Baseline (25,000) drives the sweep to 0.
- earlier_sweep_offset (parameter): a sweep entry in the twenty-four months with the record active -> the points
  swept in that window; none in it but one earlier -> every point swept. World: the 2025 sweep -> 6,000.
  Baseline 15,000.
- value_already_taken_as_store_credit (parameter, cross_difficulty=credit): the account active with a
  promotional award posted in the twelve months -> what those awards are worth at the tier's value per hundred
  points; active with awards only earlier -> what all the awards are worth at the same rate; otherwise nothing.
  Both tiers value awards the member has actually had. World: 44.00 posted 2026-06-20 -> 4,000 points. The
  near-miss is the 22.00 award of 2024-05-20, which only the whole-ledger tier would add. Baseline 13,000.

FACTOR CARD — membership_ext_points_redemption_release (5 factors; gold 23,900; whole baseline 144,200).
- live_balance_basis (method): a statement tier with a sweep entry in the twelve months -> the points earned
  inside the expiry months less what was spent and swept inside it; a statement tier with no sweep in that window
  -> the net over the thirty-six months ending on the handling day; otherwise the whole-ledger net. World: the
  sweep booked at the previous step -> 132,880 - 17,000 - 15,000 = 100,880. Baseline (144,280): 45,600.
- share_of_balance_released (parameter): a transfer out in the twelve months with the record active -> the
  transfer share 0.5; no transfer but another redemption in that window -> 0.75; otherwise the whole balance.
  World: the transfer of 2026-04-15 -> 0.5. Baseline 74,400.
- points_held_for_returns (parameter, cross_difficulty=returns): the return inspected or settled with a
  restocking fee outstanding -> that fee at the tier's value per hundred points; received or in transit with no
  fee outstanding -> the purchase price recorded on it at the same rate; otherwise nothing. Both tiers hold back
  against money the member owes or goods whose grade is not yet settled, which is what the framing sentence says,
  and both convert at the same rate as the other hold-backs. World: the Business Contract Return Schedule charges 12 per cent of the 1,200.00 line, 144.00, above its
  25.00 minimum and below its 900.00 cap; the schedule does not waive the fee for a member outright, so the
  tier's 50 per cent waiver is applied to it and 72.00 stands outstanding -> 6,545 points. Baseline 30,500.
- points_held_for_cover (parameter, cross_difficulty=protection): a deductible standing unsettled on the plan ->
  that deductible at the same rate; none unsettled but a premium standing unsettled -> that premium; otherwise
  nothing. World: the July claim was settled by repair and the plan waives the deductible on a repair, so none stands; the
  September instalment of 39.00 is unpaid -> 3,545 points. Baseline 27,500.
- points_held_for_work (parameter, cross_difficulty=service): the agreement completed with service charges
  outstanding -> those charges at the same rate; scheduled, dispatched or held for parts with labour charged in the month -> that
  labour at the same rate; otherwise nothing. World: 180.00 outstanding -> 16,364 points. Baseline 40,300.

STEP 3. WORLD. Why each class of row exists, and what changes if it goes.
- customers row: a business profile with a registered name and a tax exemption certificate, carrying the two
  locating details and the two credentials the persona states.
- membership_holdings row: Circle Business Pro standing active, activated 2019-03-15, term 2026-03-15 to
  2027-03-14, tier effective 2023-03-15, six seats in use (the schema's field carries household or business
  seats, and this tier allows ten business seats), no grace day and no lapse day. points_balance 135,200 is
  exactly the sum of the point deltas on the ledger, so nothing here is stale and the difficulty is which points
  are live rather than which figure to trust.
- nine earning entries from 2023-11-10 to 2026-08-20: they carry 42,400.00 of qualifying spend over five
  occasions inside the window, the occasion inside three months, the 24,000 points outside a thirty-month life,
  and the 132,880 earned inside the expiry months after the accrual lands. Eight name the standing supply order
  placed 2023-10-15, each a delivery instalment against it, and the ninth names the August board order; every
  one of them postdates the order it names, and the eight together come to the 79,500.00 that order was billed.
- three redemptions and two sweeps: the 2026 transfer sets the share released and the spend offset; the 2025
  sweep is the earlier-sweep offset; the 2023 sweep is the near-miss outside twenty-four months; and the absence
  of a 2026 entry is what the second prerequisite turns on.
- three purchase orders with nine order rows: the laptop order's merchandise, delivery, promotional discount
  and payment rows, the board order's line, its own delivery fee and its payment, and the supply order's
  79,500.00 line and its payment, that order reaching the service's free delivery threshold so no fee is billed.
  No sales tax is billed on any of them, the profile carrying a tax exemption certificate. Every order read
  of this task is an aggregate over these rows in a stated window, so the figures do not depend on which order a
  keyless read would have returned.
- the fleet plan and its nine rows: the July claim approved for repair, which carries no deductible charge
  because the plan waives the deductible where a claim is settled by repair, and the September instalment of
  39.00 unpaid, which is what the cover hold-back comes to on its second tier.
- the deployment agreement and its two rows: the 1,400.00 of labour is brought into the spend, its department
  decides the department bonus, and the 180.00 left outstanding after the 1,220.00 payment is held back for work.
- the business credit account and its four rows: the 44.00 promotional award of June 2026 and the 22.00 award of
  May 2024, spent, feed the two tiers of the store-credit offset.
- the return authorisation and its four rows: the machine that went back on 28 August, collected on 3 September and inspected on the 7th
  and graded open box complete, with the schedule's 144.00 restocking fee charged, 72.00 of it waived with the
  membership recorded as the reason, and the 1,200.00 merchandise refund authorised the same day and not yet
  credited to the invoice. The refund is what comes off the spend the points are earned on; the 72.00 still
  outstanding is what is held back at the redemption.
Automatic clauses: dues are annual on a 15 March anniversary and the next renewal is 2027-03-15, so no dues
charge falls due inside this call; the points cap is not reached; no benefit credit has ever been granted, so the
benefit balance of 0.00 is the sum of no deltas; the plan's unpaid premium and unsettled deductible are the
protection desk's obligations and neither lights an obligation this task set carries.

STEP 4. PERSONA. A brisk operations manager who wants the thing done and the reference for the file. Volunteered
at the opening: the laptop invoice, the order reference, the instruction to put the points against it. Given only
when asked: the registered name and postal code, the account number and the card's last four digits, the rough
figure the office once saw, the machine that went straight back because the team had over-ordered, the plan on the fleet
with something still to pay, the engineer's visit with a bill still open, the board order of August, and the
store credit from a June promotion. Reacted to only after the adviser speaks: the agreement to have whatever
needs bringing up to date sorted out, the confirmation about the order, the running of the redemption once it is
handed over, and the close. He names neither prerequisite and offers no figure but the balance the record itself
carries.

STEP 5. VERIFICATION (revision 2). Harness over the three computes at their own handling times, replaying the
real task tools between them:
  membership_ext_purchase_points_accrual        result=18080 history_rows=5  branches=30
  membership_ext_points_expiry_sweep            result=9000  history_rows=15 branches=13
  membership_ext_points_redemption_release      result=23900 history_rows=16 branches=28
  final points_balance 120380
Per-factor baseline substitution at each handling time (every factor moved the result):
  accrual: 40480 / 20000 / 22880 / 12480 / 11300 / 15820; all baselines at once 20800
  sweep: 40400 / 0 / 15000 / 13000; all baselines at once 30400
  release: 45600 / 74400 / 30500 / 27500 / 40300; all baselines at once 144200
Prerequisite sensitivity: skipping the accrual leaves the release at 14,900; skipping the sweep leaves it at
52,100; gold is 23,900. Both edges bear weight.
ORDER UNIQUENESS: both orders of the two leaves were run. Accrual then sweep gives {18080, 9000, 23900} and a
terminal DB hash beginning 6179940dbe73c130; sweep then accrual gives the same three figures and the same hash.
The reason is structural: the sweep's pool is the points earned over the whole ledger less those earned inside
the point life, and an entry dated the handling day falls inside both terms and cancels; the accrual reads the
order, return and service records and only earning-type history, which a forfeiture entry never enters; and both
writes move the running balance by addition.
Whole-input floors: zeroing the same-category history aggregates moves all three results; forcing every
cross-category read off moves all three.

STEP 6. EVALUATION. Read nodes: locate, verify, read the membership, read the whole points ledger, read the three
orders and their entries, read the plan and its ledger, read the deployment and its entries, read the credit
account and its postings, read the return and its entries. Those reads are what make both prerequisites
discoverable: the order read against the ledger read is where the agent sees that the laptop order earned
nothing, and the ledger read on its own is where the aged points and the missing sweep entry for this calendar
year become visible. Write nodes: the accrual, then the sweep, then the member's own redemption through
unlock_user_discoverable_tool -> call_user_discoverable_tool. Everything happens under one frozen_time,
2026-09-18 14:05:00 PDT.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW A CAREFUL AGENT AVOIDS THEM.
- Earning points on the machine that went back: the rule takes the refund authorised on it off the same spend.
- Taking the twelve-month window for the merchandise lines and so earning on August's board as well: 40,480.
- Earning on the gross merchandise rather than net of the promotional discount: 20,000.
- Forgetting the deployment labour, which the rule brings into the same spend: 12,480.
- Sweeping every point ever spent against the aged pool instead of the points spent in the window: nothing swept.
- Redeeming what the invoice is worth (197,727 points) rather than what the balance may release.
- Booking the redemption before the accrual or the sweep, which gives 14,900 or 52,100.
- Taking the points as a certificate when the rule says a redemption put against a charge already standing is an
  instant discount.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify. Read the membership: Circle Business Pro, active, tier effective
2023-03-15, balance 135,200. Read the ledger, the three orders and their entries, the plan, the deployment, the
credit account and the return. First the earning entry the laptop order never got: merchandise of 4,800.00 was
billed in the month with a payment taken in the same month, so the lines counted are that month's; the
promotional discount of 480.00 comes off, giving 4,320.00; the refund of 1,200.00 authorised on the machine that
went back comes off, giving 3,120.00; the completed deployment's 1,400.00 of labour joins it, giving 4,520.00;
the rate is the tier's 2.0 base plus 1.5 because the item deployed is a laptop plus 0.5 because 42,400.00 of
qualifying spend over five occasions reaches the tier's figure, that is 4.0 applied once to 4,520.00, or 18,080
points, inside the tier's cap. Then the sweep owed for the calendar year 2026: the record is active with an
occasion inside three months, so a point lives thirty months, which leaves the 24,000 earned in November 2023
outside; 5,000 spent in the last twelve months, 6,000 already swept inside twenty-four months and 4,000 whose
value was taken as a promotional award come off; 9,000 points are swept for sweep year 2026. Then the release:
the tier issues a statement and a sweep now stands in the window, so the live balance is the 132,880 earned
inside the tier's twenty-four expiry months less the 17,000 spent and the 15,000 swept inside that same window,
100,880; a transfer stands in the window so half may go, 50,440; 6,545 points are held for the 72.00 of
restocking fee still outstanding, 3,545 for the September premium instalment left unpaid on the plan — the
deductible on the July claim was waived, the claim having been settled by repair — and 16,364 for the service
charges, leaving 23,986; what stands unsettled on the profile's orders is 2,175.00, worth 197,727 points, far
more than that, so the cap does not bind; brought down to whole blocks of 100: 23,900 points, taken as an
instant discount on KES-4471-0908.

BLIND RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Working only from the documents that will be published, the tool
schemas, the rows the share tools return and the persona's lines: the request selects a points redemption against
one named invoice; the two prerequisite sentences send the reader to the earning entry the laptop order never got
and to the sweep entry owed for this calendar year; the three figures come out at 18,080, 9,000 and 23,900, with
the two prerequisites in either order. The candidates the previous revision left open are closed: every amount
held back converts at the tier's value per hundred points, so the 16,900 reading is gone; every order read is an
aggregate over a stated window, so re-serialising the rows cannot move a figure; the sweep year is defined in the
rule, so 2024 and 2025 are no longer defensible; the spend passed to the tool is the spend the rate runs on; and
the form of the redemption is fixed by a sentence of the rule.

ROUND-2 DISPOSITIONS CARRIED INTO THIS TASK. D2 and T1-4: the framing sentence and all three hold-back ladders
convert at the tier's value per hundred points, and no sentence mentions the base rate in that role. D8 and T1-3:
see CROSS-CATEGORY OBJECT DISCIPLINE above. D13 and T1-11: the accrual's baseline paragraph states the
twelve-month window, which is the ladder's fall-through, so the factor bears weight against its own honest
baseline (40,480 against 18,080). D15 and T1-12: the returns hold-back now holds back against a restocking fee
the member owes rather than against a refund Northbeam owes him; the cover and work hold-backs hold back only
amounts that genuinely stand unsettled; and the store-credit offset values only awards the member has had. D16
and T1-1: the sweep edge's sentence and condition both name a sweep entry for the calendar year the handling day
falls in, which the ledger does not carry. D17 and T1-2: the rule defines the sweep year. T1-6: the fall-through
tier of point_life_window carries a method and nothing else. T1-8: every earning entry names an order placed
before it. T1-9: the spend passed to the tool is 4,520.00, the figure the rule settles and the rate runs on.
T1-10: the rule fixes the form of a redemption put against a charge already standing, and the tool's enum gloss
for that form covers a charge as well as a till purchase. T1-13 and T1-14: this worklog's arithmetic and its
statements about the seed were re-derived from the harness run. O7: the rounding clause is named in overwrite.
O9: the plan-bonus factor is gone from this task, so the clause about the plan discount before the plan bonus
governs nothing here. O10: the overwrite of the whole-blocks clause now names the order sentence, which states a
different basis rather than repeating base. O11: the enum value the rule selects is instant_checkout_discount and
its gloss covers a charge already standing. T1-5: the seats field carries household or business seats per the
schema, and Circle Business Pro allows ten business seats, so six is within the tier's own arrangement. T1-7: the
two hold-backs that read a running quantity on another product's holding read fields the schema defines as
identically the sum of that product's ledger deltas, so the cached figure and the ledger cannot disagree; the
second tier of each now reads the ledger directly. O2 and T1-15: the redemption states its measurement window as
the expiry months of the tier and the sweep states the life a point is given, which the schedule may extend or
shorten; the two are different quantities and each rule says which it means.

ROUND-3 DISPOSITIONS CARRIED INTO THIS TASK.
N1 (the seeded restocking fee the returns charter could not produce). The return reason was wrong_item_shipped,
which returns_restocking_fee names as a ground for charging no fee at all, and the 88.00 seeded was not a figure
the schedule could reach on any reading. The reason is now business_over_ordered — the bindery ordered one
machine too many, which is what the caller says — and the figures are worked out from the schedule: 12 per cent
of the 1,200.00 line is 144.00, above its 25.00 minimum and under its 900.00 cap, and Circle Business Pro's

the reference for the file.

invoice for them is open on the business account. Kestrel has been on the Circle Business Pro membership for years
and has been collecting reward points on everything the bindery buys, and you want those points used: put whatever
the points are worth against that laptop invoice. You open with it plainly, in something like these words: "We have
the invoice for the four laptops open on the account and I want to put our Circle points against it — use whatever

gone through, reading back the reference the system gives you for the file. You do not do anything on the account
before the adviser hands it over.

You close as soon as you hear the points have gone against the laptop invoice: you say that is what you wanted, ask

argument_uniqueness_tracing.redemption_kind: instant_checkout_discount. Basis: the policy's own rule fixes the form — 'A redemption put against a charge already standing on the profile is taken as an instant discount on that charge rather than as a certificate the member spends later' — and the member asks for the points to go against the laptop invoice already open on the account. Uniqueness: reward_certificate is the form the rule expressly rules out for a charge already standing; charitable_donation would give the points to the recycling fund rather than to the invoice; points_transfer would move them to another profile, which is not what is asked.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The root has two parallel out-edges, so both orders of the two prerequisites were run. Accrual then sweep gives 18,080, 9,000 and 23,900 with a terminal DB hash beginning 6179940dbe73c130; sweep then accrual gives the same three figures and the same hash. This is structural, not luck: the sweep's aged pool is the points earned over the whole ledger less those earned inside the point life, and an entry dated the handling day falls inside both terms and cancels out; the accrual reads the order, service and plan records and only earning-type history, which a forfeiture entry never enters; and both writes move the running point balance by addition, so the terminal figure is identical either way. No policy sentence states an order between them and none is needed.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the earning entry and replaying everything else leaves the points earned inside the point life at 114,800, so the scored points_redeemed falls from 23,900 to 14,900 and the terminal ledger carries no earning entry for the laptop order.

Skipping the forfeiture and replaying everything else leaves no sweep entry in the twelve months ending on the handling day, so the live balance is read over the thirty-six months and the scored points_redeemed rises from 23,900 to 52,100; the terminal ledger also lacks the 2026 forfeiture and the balance stays 9,000 points higher.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario names neither prerequisite. The caller asks only for the points to be put against the laptop invoice; he never mentions points not having been booked, never mentions expiry, a sweep or points being lost, and never asks whether anything must be done first. His line about something needing to be brought up to date fires only after the adviser has said so, and he explicitly does not ask what it is. His one volunteered figure, about a hundred and thirty-five thousand points, is the balance the record itself carries and points at no prerequisite; his remarks about the plan, the engineer, the returned pallet and the store credit are answers to questions and name no policy, tool or order of work.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: No task tool of this difficulty validates a prerequisite. book_purchase_points_235cc6ac books its earning entry and raises the balance whatever else stands on the ledger; it reads the membership row only for the owning customer and the tier to stamp on the entry. sweep_expired_points_bcca39ef books its forfeiture and lowers the balance for any number of points, whether or not a sweep already stands for that year and whether or not the points are genuinely aged. redeem_reward_points_8621cafe books the redemption for any number of points, with no check of the balance, of the blocks, of what the points are being spent against or of anything owed on other lines, and it will drive the balance negative without complaint. Each returns its ordinary receipt in every case, so the only consequence of resolving the tree in the wrong order, or not at all, is the terminal hash.
